messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: High GPU queue growth observed in azure-eastus pool (pool=azure-eastus-gpu, queued=1860, head-latency p95=12.4s). Autoscaler attempted scale-up but hit quota errors. Pager: @oncall_james

oncall_james: saw the alert, joining. Anyone on-call for AZ eastus quota?

infra_sophie: I’m around. Quick check: autoscaler logs show repeated failures allocating VM SKUs (NVIDIA A100) due to quota limit. Error snippet from autoscaler:```
2026-03-15T02:14:12Z ERROR allocator: failed to create node: AzureError: OperationDisallowed - Subscription has reached regional vGPU quota for resource type 'Standard_ND40rs_v2'
status: 403, request-id: a1b2c3d4
```

ops_tori: Customer impact? Which routes are affected?

oncall_james: Early telemetry: high queue depth for embeddings and long-running generate routes. Some 503s returned when queue timeout hits. Not global yet but several large tenants showing error spikes. @customer-success-aly, can you confirm customer reports?

customer-success-aly: Confirmed — customer "NovaSearch" reporting intermittent 503s for embedding calls since ~02:08. They see long spikes and some failures. Logged as high-priority.

eng_runtime_lee: Autoscaler tried three scale attempts in the last 8m. Azure responded with QuotaExceeded on all. Relevant autoscaler command we run: ```
aws-like-autoscaler --region azure-eastus --pool azure-eastus-gpu --desired 24
``` But azure returned quota error so desired never reached.

infra_sophie: I queried Azure quotas quickly:```
az account show-usage --location eastus --resource-type "GPUS"
# result: Available quota for ND series: 0/4 used, limit 4 -> attempted allocation +20 -> rejected
``` Looks like we exhausted regional hard limit for that subscription.

oncall_james: Mitigation plan options: 1) Shift critical traffic to another region (uswest2) 2) Reduce concurrency / disable batching on heavy routes 3) Drain noncritical pools in eastus to free units 4) Open rapid Azure quota request (but that takes time). Thoughts?

ops_tori: I can start draining non-prod pools and scale them to 0. That should free a few GPUs if they're the same quota family. Doing: `redwood pool scale nonprod-eastus --down 0`

eng_runtime_lee: Also reduce per-worker concurrency and temporarily disable batching to reduce per-request vGPU usage: edit runtime config:```
PATCH /v1/runtime/configs/azure-eastus-gpu
{ "batching.enabled": false, "worker.max_concurrency": 1 }
``` This will increase token cost but reduces chance new jobs queue for GPUs.

oncall_james: Good. Ops, start drain now. Lee, apply the runtime changes. I’ll start traffic reroute to uswest2 for embedding-heavy tenants.

ops_tori: Draining non-prod pools now. Command output:```
> redwood pool list --region eastus
nonprod-eastus-gpu   status: draining  nodes: 6 -> 0 in progress
critical-eastus-gpu   status: active    nodes: 18
``` Expect 6 GPUs freed in ~90s.

azure-support-bot: Support case created: AZ-CC-20260315-9123. Estimated initial response 15-30m. Case notes: regional vGPU quota exceeded, requesting emergency capacity increase.

infra_sophie: After draining non-prod we freed 6 GPUs but autoscaler still hitting quota for the ND series when trying to allocate more than small amount. Might need failover.

eng_runtime_lee: I pushed a routing override for embeddings:```
redwood route update --route embeddings --from eastus --to uswest2 --weight 90 --wait 30s
``` New traffic should start shifting. Monitor the latency for uswest2 to avoid overloading that pool.

customer-success-aly: Communicated to NovaSearch: partial mitigation in progress, failover to another region, might see slightly higher latencies (~300-600ms) while warmups happen. They've acknowledged and asked for ETA; told them we'll update in 15m.

oncall_james: Let's keep public status short: "Service degradation in US (east): some embedding/generation requests may see timeouts or 503s. Mitigation in progress." Ops, send status update when routing change completes.

ops_tori: Routing change applied, traffic shifting observable. uswest2 embeddings avg latency up from 80ms -> 260ms but no 5xx spikes yet. Queue in eastus down from 1860 -> 720 after drain and routing.

eng_runtime_lee: Additional temporary config I enabled to reduce pressure: fallback to smaller model-variants on high-queue detection and stricter per-tenant rate-limits:```
if queue_length > 400: route -> model-small-quantized or return 429 for non-SLA tenants
``` Will roll this back after capacity stable.

infra_sophie: Azure support replied: initial approval might take hours for quota increase. They recommended using a separate subscription or capacity reservation for predictable peaks. Logged in case notes.

oncall_james: Summary so far: impact limited to eastus GPU pool causing queue & some 503s to large tenants. Mitigations: drained non-prod to free 6 GPUs, disabled batching + lowered concurrency, routing heavy tenants to uswest2 (weight 90), enabled model fallback and tenant rate-limits. Azure ticket AZ-CC-20260315-9123 open.

customer-success-aly: NovaSearch confirms errors decreased after failover. Still seeing some increased latencies but functional.

oncall_james: Next steps: 1) keep monitoring queues and error rates for 1 hour 2) ops to complete quota escalation with Azure, consider emergency reserved capacity 3) infra to create runbook for automated cross-region failover for quota hits 4) follow up postmortem and capacity policy. I'll hand off to night on-call @infra_sophie in 45m. Any objections?

infra_sophie: No objections. I’ll take it and own the Azure quota coordination. Will also kick off a ticket to finance for reserved capacity eval.

oncall_james: Thanks team. If anything new pops up, post here. Closing pager for me, handing to @infra_sophie. :white_check_mark:
